items.text: The new update brings a bunch of performance optimizations and the long-awaited POTATO MODE.
Now the game can run on laptops older than some of our players.
We've also added graphics presets, automatic Steam Deck detection, and a hardware benchmark to help you find the right settings for your system.
A LOT of balance changes across characters, Spells, Chips, Mementos, and Relics.
Fixes and clearer information for Unique Valuables and Bond progression.
A shorter Empyrean variation for players who have reached the top of the tower at least once.
Bug fixes, including several multiplayer issues.
Added a new, shorter variation of the Empyrean domain for players who have reached the top of the tower at least once.

This partially hidden mechanic plays a big part in the later Bond levels with the characters you meet throughout the game. We've fixed several bugs that were preventing it from working properly and added more information about how to obtain Unique Valuables.
The Pause Menu now displays both Unique Valuables and regular Valuables, such as Old World Coins. Select or hover over an item to see a tooltip with more information.
Fixed an issue where Unique Valuables could drop more than once.
Fixed an issue where higher Bond levels weren't correctly requiring their Unique Valuable.
Fixed an issue where some Unique Valuables weren't dropping correctly from chests.
We've reworked the graphics options to help the game run better on a wider range of hardware, including handheld PCs like the Steam Deck.
Added Graphics Presets so you can change all graphics settings at once.
Added a Steam Deck preset and automatic Steam Deck detection. On first launch, the game uses 1280×800 fullscreen with a 40 FPS limit.
Added Potato Mode, which lowers settings and visual effects more aggressively for lower-end hardware.
Added a hardware benchmark that recommends a graphics preset for your system.
Added an Effects Quality setting, which affects common particles and cloud quality in maps with dynamic clouds.
Optimized visual effects across the game, especially on Low and Medium settings.
Improved performance for chests and other frequently repeated objects.
We've made a broad round of balance changes and mechanic adjustments to improve the sense of progression.
Fernet and Spika: Increased early-game melee attack values by approximately 10–15%.
Laika and Dolce: Reduced early-game melee attack values by approximately 10%.
All characters: Reduced late-game melee attack values by approximately 10–15%.
Perfect Dodge follow-up damage: Reduced by 5% for Fernet, 15% for Spika, 30% for Laika, and 25% for Dolce.
Reduced late-game enemy health by approximately 5–10%.
Adjusted enemy attack cooldowns on Sinner difficulty to make enemies approximately 15% less aggressive.
Yoyo
Increased damage after dashing to the Yoyo by 50%, bringing it in line with the initial cast.
Updated Dash damage upgrades.
Doubled the Dash damage area of effect.
Solemn Guard
Curse Counter now curses enemies more easily.
Celestial Transposition
Evasion of Time upgrades now slow enemies for an additional 0.5 seconds.
Increased Evasion of Time II's range and chance to apply slowdown.
The Overdash upgrade can now trigger without hitting an enemy.
Fernet
Increased Raiquen's overall damage by 20%.
Increased Raiquen's “Attack in Place” damage by 50%.
Spika
Increased Sangetsu's damage at higher levels by approximately 10–15%.
Increased Shin Sangetsu's overall damage by 20%.
Increased Higanbana's damage at higher levels by approximately 10%.
Reduced Mahou Spika's Higanbana Nidai damage by approximately 25%.
Laika
Increased Damocles' Weight of Sin III damage bonus: 25% → 50%.
Increased Damocles' Slam damage by 50%.
Increased Mahou Laika's Bear Sprint damage by approximately 200%.
Bear Sprint now pushes enemies out of its path.
Dolce
Increased Curtain Call's explosion damage by 10%.
Mahou Dolce now spawns one Copia per cast. It lasts 10 seconds before detonating into Curtain Call.
Mahou Dolce no longer leaves Copias behind after performing a dodge roll.
Small Defense, Health, and Attack Chips: Reduced costs: 25 → 20.
Medium Attack: Reduced attack bonus: 40% → 25%.
Big Attack: Reduced attack bonus: 50% → 40%.
MultiThreading: Reduced health bonus: 40 → 20.
Final Form: Reduced Memory cost: 100 → 40.
Essence Purifier: Reduced Memory cost: 30 → 20.
Soul Canisters: Soul capacity now scales with the player's level.
Swift Learner: Souls granted now scale with the player's level.
MagikaBoost: Increased cost and Memory requirements. Increased Magika recovery: 10% → 20%.
MagikaBoostStr: Increased Magika recovery: 20% → 40%.
Big Defense: Reduced defense bonus: 40% → 30%.
Aerial Dancer: Reduced bonus damage: 35% → 30%.
Relic Collector: Increased damage bonus per Relic: 3% → 4%.
Self Healing Protocol: Nearly halved cost and Memory requirements, and doubled healing to 0.5% per second.
Shared Magik Circuit: Increased activation distance by 15%.
Treasure Hunter: Reduced unlock cost: 100 → 30 coins.
Erika's Pride: Reduced Sin Meter-based damage by 40%.
Laika's Rancor: Increased activation distance by 40%.
Nakshatra's Lust: Reduced stacks gained from finishers, halved stacks gained at Level II, and slightly reduced the activation radius.
Ranka's Quest: Reduced bonus damage per Wish by approximately 20%. Swapped Level II and III rewards; the attack bonus is now granted at Level III.
Pebble Bounty: Increased pebble bonus damage: 5% → 10%.
AetherStrike: Doubled shield gains at Levels I, II, and III.
Airy's Revenge: Increased Level II slash damage by approximately 10%.
Flask of Souls: Souls granted now scale with the player's level.
Crystal Heart: Reduced bonus HP: 15 → 10.
Oxizakre: Increased extra healing: 20% → 33%.
Odin's Orb: Reduced free cast chance: 25% → 20%.
Philosopher's Stone: Reduced Magika regeneration per Relic by 10%.
Pixie Dust Jar: Reduced kills required to activate: 20 → 10. Reduced healing: 50 → 30.
Germ Devourer: Reduced healing per kill: 10 → 5.
Boots of Avarice: Expanded the description.
Symbol of Faith: Updated the description.
Death: Reduced Wishes granted per level-up: 3 → 2.
Flan's Gluttony: Doubled Level III healing per second.
Velvet Guillotine: Increased Level II execution chance: 7.5% → 10%. Changed the Level III effect: every 3 executions grant 3 Critical Hits.
Pandora's Projectiles: Reduced damage by approximately 10%.
Aspect of Copper: Increased Heavencrawl chance: 5% → 20%.
Valkyrie Portrait: The description now correctly displays its 33% healing chance. Healing per Lost Wish now scales with the Sin Meter percentage.
Berserker Soul: The combo required to become Empowered now decreases each time Berserker Soul activates.
Dream Chaser: Reduced the base damage bonus to Perfect Dodge follow-up attacks: 100% → 30%. Now grants an additional 3% damage bonus to Perfect Dodge follow-ups for each Coffin Purified.
Fixed UI markers disappearing when a multiplayer client changed characters.
Fixed an issue where an elevator could fall onto the player after defeating a mid-boss.
Fixed an issue in Heart of Heaven where multiplayer clients could become stuck on a white screen after falling from platforms while the group was travelling to the final stage.
Fixed Caius' promise rejection dialogue incorrectly displaying Raiza's name.
Fixed tutorial camera views displaying black bars on some aspect ratios.
Hey everyone!
Akira, Kernel Hearts director here.
It's been almost a month since the game came out, and today we're happy to release our first content patch!

We dug into your feedback to identify some of the most requested features and improvements. We still have work to do, but I'm happy we could get this out ahead of our original estimate of late October.
This means that almost everything on the October Roadmap is now out, except for the English voiceover!
We've added a training mode that's accessible right after finishing the tutorial.
Here, you'll be able to experiment with any Mementos, Relics, and enemies you've come across during your expeditions. There's also a very fun vertical movement challenge. What a thrill.

Originally, we wanted the tutorial to be brief, but we found that some folks left the initial level with more questions than answers. We've expanded the tutorial to cover almost all of the game's mechanics, including some secrets. The tutorial can now also be replayed from the Main Menu.
We're trying something new here, so all feedback is welcome, especially from folks who struggled with the original version.
You can now have up to 3 save slots! You'll also be able to check your progress for each save on the save slot screen from the Main Menu.
You can now have up to four preset chipsets, so you can easily switch between them before an expedition.
You'll now get the chance to re-roll the spell offered on the Level Up screen. Gone are the days of yearning for Links of Blood.

We've taken your feedback and greatly expanded the keybinding options, alongside lots of bug fixes and improved support for different types of controllers. You can also select the button icons that best match your controller.
Frame rate is no longer capped at the monitor's refresh rate.
Added a setting on PC to choose which controller's button icons are shown.
Added a resolution quality setting.
Display setting changes must now be confirmed after they're applied.
Mahou Transformation can now be rebound on keyboard.
Movement keys (WASD) can now be rebound.
The Toggle HUD key can now be rebound.
The Emote Wheel can now be rebound.
The Chip Menu now highlights newly discovered chips and shows them all before giving control to the player.
Chips available to acquire now display their memory cost.
Chips you can currently afford to acquire have a shining lock icon.
The Continue button is now the first option in the Main Menu and is hidden when there's no game to continue.
Increased the base Heavy Attack string's damage against shields.
Decreased Jawbreaker's damage against shields.
Reduced Heavy Attack 2's recovery from 24 to 16 frames.
Heavy Attack 2 now causes hitstop on its first hit.
Reduced hitbox sizes throughout the Heavy Attack string.
Increased Moon Lander's recovery from 18 to 20 frames.
Reduced Moon Lander's hitbox size.
Increased Fist-Mode Heavy Attack 3's damage from 27 to 42.
Fist-Mode Running Light Attack can now be cancelled into a dash.
Combo enders in Fist-Mode now allow you to restart their strings sooner.
Removed Full Moon's startup invincibility frames.
Redistributed Full Moon's hitboxes around Spika.
Full Moon now only staggers the enemy in front of Spika.
Reduced Full Moon's damage from 11 to 7 for hits around Spika.
Increased Full Moon's damage from 22 to 24 for the hit in front of Spika.
Increased Full Moon's number of hits from 5 to 9.
Slightly reduced Overhead's hitbox size.
Decreased mana recovery from airborne attacks.
Increased mana recovery from Heavy Attacks.
Increased mana recovery from Chasing the Beatle.
Increased the pushback distance of Higanbana's final slash.
Fixed an issue that caused air attacks to deal the same damage regardless of distance to enemies.
Fixed inconsistencies when trying to continue a combo string after casting Copia.
Shortened Redemption's cancel window.
Increased Redemption's damage per loop from 19 to 30.
Increased Heavy Attack 1's damage from 96 to 144 at its farthest hitbox.
Increased Light Attack damage at mid and long range. Damage at the farthest hitbox is now:
Light Attack 1: 35 → 40
Light Attack 2: 36 → 44
Light Attack 3: 36 → 42
Light Attack 4: 43 → 48
Dash animations can now be cancelled into jumps.
Slightly increased Soul rewards from Coffin Purification in all levels.
Slightly increased the time required for the Sin Meter to reach 100% in all levels.
Slightly reduced Soul rewards from enemies and Stray Souls in Skybound Citadel, Twisted Halls, and Judecca.
Moderately reduced Heavencrawl's effectiveness on bosses.
Slightly reduced the number of enemies that spawn per door in Judecca.
Reduced the hitbox size of Kadmiel's bite attack.
Reduced the hitbox size of the third hit in Cursed Ronin's 3-hit combo.
Reduced the starting enemy level in Skybound Citadel by 1.
Moderately reduced Warden Angel's shield points.
Slightly increased Warden Angel's health.
Slightly reduced Envoy Elite's health.
Slightly reduced Bomber Elite's health.
Slightly reduced Juggernaut's health.
Moderately reduced Ground Master's shield points.
Slightly increased Ground Master's health.
Slightly reduced Cursed Ronin's shield points.
Slightly increased Cursed Ronin's health.
Fixed an issue that prevented Armorial Angel from receiving bonus damage from Heavy Attacks.
The "Hoarder" achievement can now be unlocked. Players who already qualify will get it the next time they start the game.
The "Stocked" achievement now requires every chip. It no longer unlocks a few chips early.
Dolce's air attacks now deal more damage at longer range, as intended.
Fixed an animation glitch when cancelling out of Dolce's Copia.
Fixed Dolce's whip appearing during her Burst animation.
Fixed Aether Strike affecting the player who used it and causing slowdown.
Ichigo's Trick now slows down the enemy it triggers on.
Kira's Wrath executions now trigger from Dolce's long-range whip hits.
Heartstopper now respects its cooldown.
Heartstopper now releases enemies when the player moves away from them.
Heartstopper's mark is now visible when the same enemy is marked again.
Fixed Soulbloom taking too long to die.
Fixed players being able to get out of bounds in the tutorial, including with Fernet's Yo-Yo.
Fixed players being able to get out of bounds in Ash Desert.
Fixed players being able to get past the collapsed hallway debris after Nura's Fire Exit bond.
Fixed a shiny floor surface in Twisted Halls that caused visual glitches.
Fixed chip buttons in the Chip Menu sometimes staying tinted or invisible.
The Memento and Level Up menus now display correctly on ultrawide and other screen sizes.
Fixed the Promise menu's accept button being out of place.
Fixed D-pad presses registering twice on PlayStation and Switch Pro controllers.
Fixed an issue where only the first gamepad was registered for input.
Fixed lag in multiplayer caused by the Sin Meter.
Fixed player deaths sometimes not registering for everyone in multiplayer.
Fixed screen flickering when motion blur is turned off.

releases.displayName: Kernel Hearts Release Date + Demo Update

items.text: Hey everyone, Akira here, Game Director of Kernel Hearts.
Today, I'm very happy to announce that Kernel Hearts will be launching one month from now, on September 17th!
To celebrate, we decided to update the Demo one last time before release.
Japanese VO has been added to the game!
Make sure to start a New Game to enjoy all the story scenes with the new Japanese voice acting.
Attending these recording sessions was a dream come true for me. Watching the actors bring these characters to life was incredibly fun, and easily one of the highlights of this year.
We've listened to a lot of your feedback, and as a result we've done some pretty significant rebalancing across both the game's combat and economy.
For combat, we've adjusted most Mementos and Relics so they scale better with player level, while also rebalancing them to make every choice feel more rewarding to use.

Some of the ones that rely more heavily on scaling might still miss the mark a little in the Demo because of its shorter runs, but hopefully the overall feeling of getting stronger throughout a run feels much better now.
Keep in mind that the Demo only has 2 floors, while the full game has around 7! Things are expected to get considerably crazier later in a full run than what we're able to show during Demo sessions.
We've also adjusted enemy numbers throughout the game to make encounters feel less spongy while still maintaining the level of challenge we're aiming for.

On the economy side, we've made exploring and fighting the random enemies around the map much more rewarding. They now have a significantly higher chance of dropping Lost Wishes, alongside an overall rebalance of chest loot tables.
We've removed the placeholder translations and are now only keeping the professionally translated languages in the Demo.

Some players asked us to keep the placeholders because they still helped them play the game even if they knew little or no English, but we also don't want new players to see those translations and assume they represent the quality we're aiming for in the final game.
So for now, we'd rather only include languages that properly reflect the experience we want to deliver.
We've improved a lot of the UI to make it feel sharper and more responsive, alongside updates and improvements to many enemy VFX.
We've also been working extensively on improving performance throughout the game.
So far we've seen some pretty significant improvements, and the game should now run considerably better on lower-end PCs.
If you have a potato PC and want to help us test it, please get in touch with us on Discord and let us know how it runs!
As always, thank you so much to everyone who took the time to read this, play the Demo, and send us feedback.
I also encourage you to check out the latest trailer we've made. It's a bit slower-paced than some of our previous ones, but I think it turned out very cool.
See you in Babel!
